did.abstract: Charles R. Eisendrath (b. 1940), is a former Time magazine correspondent and professor of journalism at the University of Michigan. He is director emeritus of the Wallace House Center for Journalists at the University of Michigan. This collection consists of the professional records of Charles R. Eisendrath, mostly from his time working at the University of Michigan.

accessrestrict.p: This collection is open without restriction.

acqinfo.p: Donated by the Wallace House Center for Journalists (donor no. 11568) in August 2016 and July 2018.

arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into four series: Professional activity, Teaching files, Health policy work, and Writings.

bioghist.head: Biographical Note
bioghist.p: Charles R. Eisendrath (b. 1940) is an emeritus professor of communications studies and former director of the Wallace House Center for Journalists at the University of Michigan. Eisendrath received a BA from Yale University in 1962 and an MA from the University of Michigan in 1965. He began his professional career in journalism reporting for the St. Louis Post-Dispatch and Baltimore Evening Sun before joining Time magazine as a correspondent. There he earned national attention covering the Chilean coup that overthrew the government of Salvador Allende. Eisendrath later became bureau chief in Buenos Aires, overseeing all news operations in South America. He has appeared on National Public Radio and Good Morning America, and his writing has appeared in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Atlantic, and many other publications.

Eisendrath joined the U-M faculty in 1975 as an assistant professor of journalism. In 1981 he became the founding director of the Livingston Awards, a prize for young journalists, and he became the third director of the Knight-Wallace Fellowship for Journalists in 1986. Under Eisendrath's leadership, the organiziation grew an endowment of over $60 million and brokered a donation by renowned journalist Mike Wallace of the arts-and-crafts style house that would become the organization's permanent headquarters.

Eisendrath also held an interest in health policy, working with the Transplant and Health Policy Center and serving on the U-M Genome Ethics Committee from 1993-1995. Moreover, in December of 2000, Eisendrath and his family miraculously survived a plane crash over Costa Rica, sustaining signficant injuries that required long-term medical care. Eisendrath channelled this personal experience into his interest in health policy: the differences in patient care that he observed between the medical systems of U-M and the Mayo Clinic prompted him to kick start the Michigan Model Care Initiative with Michigan Medicine's chief medical officer, Dr. Darrell "Skip" Campbell. The program aimed to establish standards for cross-specialty communication and coordination within the U-M system, with hopes that other teaching and research hospitals would emulate the paradigm.

Eisendrath was involved in many other administrative activities at U-M, including serving multiple terms on the Clements Library Associate Board of Governors. Eisendrath retired from U-M in 2016 after serving nearly 30 years as director of the Wallace House.

relatedmaterial.p: The Bentley Historical Library houses the following related collections: Wallace House Center for Journalists (University of Michigan) records.

scopecontent.p: This collection consists of the professional records of Charles R. Eisendrath, primarily during his time working at the University of Michigan.

The Professional activity series is comprised of administrative records and correspondence relating both to various committees on which Eisendrath served and to external professional organizations in which he was involved, including the International Press Institute, Council of Michigan Foundations, and more. Also included are general professional correspondence and born-digital records of his professional activities.
The Teaching series includes material related to journalism courses taught by Eisendrath such as syllabi and supplementary assignment material.

The Health Policy series includes administrative records and correspondence related to Eisendrath's work on health policy with various organziations, including the Transplant and Health Policy Center, the U-M Committee on Genome Ethics, and the Michigan Model Care Initiative (MMCI). Also included are records relating to his plane crash (the event which led to his involvement with MMCI), comprising published writings about the event and correspondence following the event and the beginnings of MMCI.
The Writings series consists of research files and drafts of written works, including a significant amount of material pertaining to the legal trials of the French newspaper, Le Monde.
